title: Establishment and long-term culture of mouse mammary stem cell organoids and breast tumor organoids
protocol: Euthanize mice according to the protocol approved by the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee.
Harvest the #2, 3 & 4 mammary fat pads from euthanized mice.
Wash mammary fat pads in ice-cold PBS in a sterile conical tube.
Mince the washed mammary fat pads into ∼1 mm³ pieces using a sterile blade.
Transfer minced mammary fat pad pieces to a new 15 mL tube with Gland Digestion Buffer I per mouse.
Incubate the digestion mixture on a nutator at 37°C for 1.5 - 2 hours.
Harvest tumors (∼1 cm in diameter) from euthanized mice.
Wash tumors in ice-cold PBS in a sterile conical tube.
Mince the washed tumors into ∼1 mm³ pieces using a sterile blade.
Transfer minced tumor pieces to a new 15 mL tube with Tumor Digestion Buffer I per mouse.
Incubate the digestion mixture on a nutator at 37°C for 2 hours.
Add 5 ml of PBS to each tube containing digested tissue from mammary fat pads or tumors after incubation.
Pipette up and down the tissue mixture in each tube twenty times.
Centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 min at 4°C–8°C.
Carefully aspirate the supernatant (fatty top layer and liquid layer).
Do not disturb the cell pellet.
For mammary epithelial cell isolation: this step is optional.
If yield is important, perform red blood cell lysis.
For each mouse, add 1 mL RBC lysis, resuspend cell pellet, and place tube on ice for 1 min.
After 1 min, pipet the cell mixture up and down gently for 5–6 times.
Add 10 mL PBS to the tube and spin down at 500 × g for 5 min.
If yield is not an issue (like in large preps), resuspend the pellet with 10 mL PBS by pipetting, pulse spin at 1,000 × g for 1 min.
Remove the supernatant containing red blood cells.
For tumor organoid cell isolation: perform RBC lysis as above.
Resuspend cell pellets in 1 mL 0.05% trypsin-EDTA, place the tube at 37°C for 5 min, mixing occasionally by shaking.
After 5 min, pipet the cell mixture to dissociate clumps.
Add 10 mL basic medium II to stop the digestion and centrifuge at 700 × g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellets with 1 mL Digestion Buffer II by pipetting and incubate for 5 min at 37°C with occasional mixing by shaking.
After 5 min, pipet the cell mixture to dissociate clumps.
Add 10 mL PBS to stop the digestion.
Centrifuge at 700 × g for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend with 3 mL Suspension Buffer.
Filter through 40 μm cell strainers to obtain single cells.
Mix 0.1 mL cell suspension with 0.1 mL 0.4% trypan blue.
Count live cells using a Hemocytometer, noting that live cells do not take up trypan blue.
Wash cells with organoid culture medium before plating.
Centrifuge the tube at 700 × g for 5 minutes to pellet down the cell suspension.
Resuspend the pellet in fresh ice-cold organoid culture medium containing 5% Matrigel.
Resuspend the cell pellet in ice-cold organoid culture medium containing 5% Matrigel at a final concentration of 150,000 cells per mL.
Seed 300,000 cells with 2 mL of culture medium into one well of poly-HEMA coated 6-well plates.
Place the plate in a humidified incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2 for organoid culture.
Replace the medium every 3 days.
Check organoid growth under a light microscope.
After 4–6 days, organoids greater than 100 μm in diameter should form.
Thaw Matrigel on ice.
Collect organoids into a 15 mL tube containing 10 mL of ice-cold PBS by pipetting the Matrigel layer containing organoids.
Mix and centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 minutes.
Digest organoids with 0.05% Trypsin-EDTA (1 mL per well) for 5–10 minutes at 37°C.
Gently pipette up and down during digestion to ensure uniformity.
Add 10 mL of Basic medium II to stop the trypsinization process.
Centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 minutes.
Remove supernatant without disturbing the pellet.
Resuspend cell pellet in 3 mL Basic medium II.
Do cell counting.
Seed cells using organoid culture medium at different cell densities depending on experimental aims.
For passage, seed 300,000 cells with 2 ml organoid medium per well for 6-well plates.
For quantifying organoid-forming efficiency, seed 200–500 cells per well in 96-well plates.
Passage the culture when the majority of organoids are between 100–200 μm in diameter.
Refresh medium every 3–4 days.
Prepare freezing medium before the experiment.
Dissociate organoids into single cells based on steps 11–15.
Resuspend the cell pellet with 3 mL of freezing medium (for the cell pellet from one well of a 6-well plate).
Transfer 1 mL of cell suspension into a cryovial.
Place the vial in a slow-freezing container and put it at -80°C freezer.
The following day, transfer the frozen cryovials to the liquid nitrogen tank for long-term storage.
Mix 20 mg of low-melting agarose with 1 mL of water in a 2 mL tube.
Put the tube in a heat block set at 70°C to melt the agarose.
Let the agarose solution cool down to about 45°C–50°C.
Centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Add 1 mL of 4% PFA or 10% formalin to fix the organoids for 30 minutes on ice.
Add 10 mL PBS to the tube and centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Repeat step (fixation and washing) twice.
Resuspend the organoids in 1 mL of 0.1% BSA/PBS.
Transfer the resuspended organoids to a 1.5 mL tube.
Centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Coat the bottom of a cryomold (10 × 10 × 5 mm) with a layer of 2% agarose by adding 100 μL per cryomold and spreading it gently with the pipette tip.
Cool down the agarose at 22°C–25°C for 5 minutes.
Gently mix the organoids from step (resuspension and centrifugation) with 100 μL of 2% agarose solution using a P200 pipette tip with the end cut off to avoid bubbles.
Place the organoids/agarose mixture into the agarose-coated cryomold using a cut P200 tip, ensuring it is in the middle of the mold.
Return the cryomold to ice for 10–20 minutes until the gel solidifies completely.
Gently and carefully remove the solidified agarose containing the embedded organoids from the mold.
Transfer the solidified agarose into a tissue cassette for further processing.
Proceed with the paraffin embedding process following the standard FFPE protocol.
Add 1 mL of 30% sucrose solution to the organoid pellet.
Place the sucrose-containing pellet at 4°C overnight (12–16 hours).
Remove as much sucrose as possible from the pellet.
Place a few drops of OCT onto the center of the cryomold.
Mix approximately 300 μL of OCT with the organoid pellet gently.
Transfer the OCT/organoid mixture into the OCT drop in the cryomold using a cut 200 µL pipette tip.
Remove any air bubbles that occur in the tissue mold with a pipette tip.
Carefully add more OCT onto the specimen until it is completely covered, avoiding any bubbles inside the OCT.
Snap freeze the block in liquid nitrogen.
Store frozen blocks at -80°C.
Cut 10 μm thick sections using a cryostat.
Pass the tissue slides through 100% Xylene I for 5 minutes.
Pass the tissue slides through 100% Xylene II for 5 minutes.
Pass the tissue slides through Xylene/ethanol (1:1, v/v) for 5 minutes.
Pass the tissue slides through 100% ethanol for 5 minutes.
Pass the tissue slides through 95% ethanol for 5 minutes.
Pass the tissue slides through 75% ethanol for 5 minutes.
Pass the tissue slides through 50% ethanol for 5 minutes.
Wash the slides with water for 5 minutes twice.
Incubate slides in antigen unmasking buffer and perform antigen retrieval using a retriever.
Allow the tissues to cool down to 25°C after about 2-3 hours of processing.
Wash the slides with water for 5 minutes twice.
Encircle the section with a hydrophobic barrier pen.
Incubate the section in blocking buffer (3% BSA, 0.1% TritonX-100 in PBS) for 1 hour at 22°C–25°C.
Discard the blocking buffer.
Incubate the section in diluted primary antibody in 3% BSA of PBS overnight (12–16 hours) at 4°C in the dark.
Wash with 0.1% Tween-20/PBS for 5 minutes, repeating 3 times with shaking.
Incubate the sections in fluorescent-dye conjugated secondary antibody diluted in 3% BSA of PBS for 1 hour at 22°C–25°C in the dark.
Wash the slides with 0.1% Tween-20/PBS for 5 minutes, repeating 3 times with shaking.
Mount coverslip with mounting medium (with DAPI).
Capture images under confocal microscopy.
Coat 10 cm plates with 20 μg/mL collagen I in PBS for 1 hour at 22°C–25°C.
Split HEK293T cells 1:4 from 90% confluent culture to the collagen I-coated plates using transfection medium.
Prepare the transfection mixture in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Mix DNA in the following ratio (details not provided).
For a 10 cm plate, dilute DNA to 600 μL jetPrime buffer and mix well.
Add 12 μL jetPrime reagent, vortex for 10 seconds, spin briefly.
Incubate the transfection mixture for 10 minutes at 22°C–25°C.
Add transfection mixture to cells.
Refresh transfection medium after 4–5 hours.
Refresh transfection medium on Day 3 with 10 mL per 10 cm plate.
Add new medium dropwise onto cells on Day 3.
Collect viral supernatant in a 50 mL tube on Day 4.
Add fresh transfection medium to the collected supernatant.
Repeat step d on Day 5.
Collect viral supernatant again on Day 6.
Filter collected virus through a 0.45 μm filter.
Aliquot and freeze filtered virus at -80°C for long-term storage if not used within 1 week.
Resuspend 300,000 cells with 1 mL virus-containing medium on Day 1 of lentiviral infection.
Supplement the medium with 5 μg/mL polybrene.
Refresh organoid culture medium after overnight (12–16 h) infection.
Refresh organoid culture medium and supplement with a selection antibiotic on Day 3.
